claims.text: Panama-flagged bulk carrier M.V. Ocean Winner sank in the Bay of Bengal off the coast of Odisha.
M.V. Ocean Winner had 24 crew members onboard, comprising 20 Chinese nationals, three Myanmarese nationals, and one Bangladeshi national.
M.V. Ocean Winner departed Paradip Port late on August 20, 2026, carrying iron ore.
Communication with M.V. Ocean Winner was lost 36 hours after its departure, prompting a search and rescue request to the Maritime Rescue Coordination Centre.
An Indian Navy P8I surveillance aircraft detected two floating liferafts and an oil slick near the reported position of M.V. Ocean Winner.
Commercial vessel MT Aisopos rescued two Chinese crew members from liferafts by late evening on August 22, 2026.
Equasis database records show M.V. Ocean Winner was a 28-year-old vessel built in 1998, measuring 225 metres long and 32.26 metres wide, with a capacity of around 73,000 tonnes.
An inspection of M.V. Ocean Winner in Chittagong, Bangladesh, in June reported three deficiencies, including one with its magnetic compass.
M.V. Ocean Winner's current owner is based in Fujian, China, and the vessel is covered by Protection and Indemnity insurance effective from August 1, 2026.
Union Shipping and Waterways Minister Sarbananda Sonowal confirmed that two survivors were rescued and provided medical care.
M.V. Ocean Winner sank approximately 230 to 240 nautical miles off the coast while carrying 72,100 metric tonnes of iron ore.
M.V. Ocean Winner departed the Paradip coast at 10:42 pm on August 20, carrying iron ore fines.
Initial reports from Indian maritime authorities stated M.V. Ocean Winner was bound for China, while other government information indicated Singapore as its destination.
The Andaman & Nicobar Command reported that M.V. Ocean Winner sent a distress alert on Saturday from a position around 300 nautical miles north-northwest of Diglipur.
Victory Star Group Co Ltd requested search and rescue assistance after communication with M.V. Ocean Winner was lost late on August 22.
The Indian Coast Guard deployed vessels ICGS Varad, ICGS Anmol, and ICGS Vijit to assist in search operations.
Coast Guard spokesperson Commandant Amit Uniyal reported that rough sea conditions in the Bay of Bengal were hampering search operations.
In September 2009, the Mongolian-flagged bulk carrier MV Black Rose sank near Paradip after developing a hull leak while carrying 23,847 tonnes of iron ore.
In 2009, the MV Asian Forest capsized off Mangalore Port on India's west coast due to cargo liquefaction after loading iron ore fines.
